name.text: RMS Book - Ch1Q4 - Before collecting more data

questiontext.text:
Mission 4: Spend the research budget wisely

A maize research team is considering a new study. Existing trials have already established a general irrigation response, and 25 years of daily climate records may be available.

[[if test="is(scenario=0)"]]

The team wants to understand how maize performance could vary across unusually dry years. The available climate records are sufficiently complete, and a crop model has been appropriately validated for the intended use.

[[else]]

The team wants to understand which variety characteristics farmers consider important, but the team does not yet know the relevant categories.

[[/if]]

Which next step is best justified by the stated knowledge gap?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

[[hint title="What would make this study worthwhile?"]]

Choose the method that resolves the stated uncertainty, rather than assuming a new field trial is always necessary.

[[/hint]]

generalfeedback.text:
[[if test="is(scenario=0)"]]

Answer: 2. Existing climate data and a suitably validated model can help explore variation across years without automatically requiring a new trial for every year. Check access, completeness and suitability before using records.

[[else]]

Answer: 3. When the relevant farmer priorities are unknown, open discussions can uncover them before a fixed-response survey or a tightly specified experiment is designed.

[[/if]]

The method follows the uncertainty that remains, not the team's disciplinary habits.
